newsitem.title: USA: Judge likely to deny Honda class-action bid.
newsitem.headline: Judge likely to deny Honda class-action bid.

text.p: In a setback to scores of dealers suing American Honda Motor Co., a federal judge in Baltimore said Friday he will most likely deny their bid to achieve class-action status.

The decision by U.S. District Judge Frederick Motz -- if reaffirmed at an Aug. 6 hearing -- means that Honda Motor Co. Ltd.'s exposure to potential damages from the lawsuits would be greatly diminished.

More than 60 U.S. Honda and Acura dealers have sued the Japanese automaker following a recent kickback scandal that resulted in 21 criminal convictions of American Honda managers and dealers for fraud and perjury.

Most of the suits allege that American Honda, the automaker's U.S. sales arm, was responsible for two decades of management corruption, during which certain dealers received unfairly generous vehicle allocations and additional franchises by bribing company officials.

Had Motz certified the suits as a single class action, it could have automatically included nearly all of Honda's more than 1,200 dealers, pushing potential damages into the billions of dollars. Without the class-action designation, the suits will proceed as separate actions.
Honda's American depositary receipts fell $3.25 on the New York Stock Exchange to close at $60.06 Friday, largely due to investor concern over the ruling.
Motz "told the parties that he was leaning against certification," said Craig Wolff, a law clerk in Motz' office. "He said he felt pretty strongly on the issue."
Wolff said Motz cited several reasons for the preliminary decision, including the presence of too many divergent interests that outweighed the suits' common claims.
In a statement, Honda said it was very pleased with the preliminary ruling.

"Honda vigorously opposes these civil cases being certified as a class action because the facts and circumstances of each of these cases is unique," the company said. "The court will issue its final decision on Aug. 6."
The lead plaintiffs attorney in the case was not immediately available for comment on Motz' remarks.
